lines.japanese: 朝方。
lines.english: Early morning.

lines.japanese: 夜勤を終えて、俺は羽田の家に帰ってきた。
lines.english: My night shift over, I came home to the Haneda house.

lines.japanese: 「お、おはようございます」
lines.english: “G-good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「ういーっす」
lines.english: “Mornin'.”

lines.japanese: 登校前の小鳩に遭遇。居間で朝食を摂っていた。
lines.english: I ran into Kobato before school. She was eating breakfast in the living room.

lines.japanese: 「いつも遅くまでごくろうさまです」
lines.english: “Thank you for always working so late.”

lines.japanese: 「どーも。つっても、とくべつ他人より苦労はしてねーよ」
lines.english: “Sure. Though it's not like I work any harder than anybody else.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、てつやでお仕事するのは、とてもたいへんなことです」
lines.english: “No, working all night without sleeping is very hard.”

lines.japanese: 「徹夜でお仕事するより、早起きしてガッコ行く方のが偉いって」
lines.english: “Getting up early and going to school is more impressive than working through the night.”

lines.japanese: カンテツならともかく、このあとフツーに寝るしな俺の場合。単に活動時間が逆転してるだけの話だ。
lines.english: It'd be one thing if I stayed up around the clock, but I was going to sleep normally after this. My waking hours were just flipped around.

lines.japanese: 「人間はやこうせいの動物なので、朝おきるのは当たりまえのことです」
lines.english: “Humans are nocturnal animals, so waking up in the morning is only natural.”

lines.japanese: ホモサピエンスが夜行性の動物だったとは初耳だが、ともあれ俺を持ちあげたいという気持ちは伝わってきた。
lines.english: It was news to me that *Homo sapiens* were nocturnal, but at least I understood that she was trying to build me up.

lines.japanese: 小鳩のフォローはフォローになっていない場合が多い。しかしそこに悪意はないと分かるので、思わず微笑ましい気持ちになってしまう。
lines.english: Kobato's attempts to help often didn't help. But I knew there was never any malice behind them, which made them oddly endearing.

lines.japanese: 「はやおきは二束三文の得っていいいます」
lines.english: “They say the early bird gets three measly pennies.”

lines.japanese: 「ソレ、そんな半端な数字だったっけ。十六文ぐらいじゃなかったっけ」
lines.english: “Was it really that lousy a number? I thought it was something like sixteen.”

lines.japanese: 「それは大っきいプロレスラーのひとです」
lines.english: “That’s the big wrestler’s Sixteen-Mon Kick.”

lines.japanese: どうでもいい。なんにせよ俺には無縁のことわざだ。
lines.english: Whatever. Either way, the proverb had nothing to do with me.

lines.japanese: 頬の裏を舌で撫でながら、小鳩の正面に腰を下ろした。
lines.english: I sat down across from Kobato, running my tongue along the inside of my cheek.

lines.japanese: 「あ、朝ごはん食べますか」
lines.english: “Oh, would you like breakfast?”

lines.japanese: やつが立ちあがりながら言った。
lines.english: She spoke as she stood.

lines.japanese: 「んーと……」
lines.english: “Let's see...”

lines.japanese: 俺が返事するより早くキッチンへ駆けだしてる。
lines.english: Before I could answer, she was already hurrying into the kitchen.

lines.japanese: 「悪り。準備できてなきゃいいけど」
lines.english: “Sorry. Don't go to any trouble if nothing's ready.”

lines.japanese: 「だいじょぶです、電子レンジは主婦のみかたです」
lines.english: “It's okay. The microwave is a housewife's best friend.”

lines.japanese: てきぱきと動きはじめた。
lines.english: She set to work with brisk efficiency.

lines.japanese: ありがたい。ほんとにクタクタのときは食欲さえ麻痺するけど、ちょうど昨晩くらいの疲労度なら仕事明けは結構な空腹だ。
lines.english: I appreciated it. When I was truly exhausted, even my appetite went numb, but after a night about as tiring as the last one, I came off work pretty damn hungry.

lines.japanese: なかなか時間は合わないけど、だからこそ、小鳩とは可能なかぎりいっしょにメシを食おうと思っている。
lines.english: Our schedules rarely lined up, which was exactly why I tried to eat with Kobato whenever I could.

lines.japanese: いずれ消えゆく身だったころとは違うんだ。もうヨージもタカシもいない──小鳩にとっては、もう俺しかいないんだ。
lines.english: Things were different from when I'd expected to vanish someday. Youji and Takashi were gone now—Kobato had no one left but me.

lines.japanese: この先の長い人生、ずっと俺が小鳩の家族になるんだ。
lines.english: For the long life ahead of her, I would always be Kobato's family.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あ、ああああのう、すみません……」
lines.english: “Um, um, u-u-um, I'm sorry...”

lines.japanese: だけど、なんでか俺、このチビっ子に恐がられてンだよな……。
lines.english: But for some reason, this little kid was scared of me...

lines.japanese: 「い、いま冷ぞう庫見たら、成田さんの好きなお肉系がぜんめつしてて……」
lines.english: “I-I just looked in the refrigerator, and all the meat dishes you like are completely gone...”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ、いいって、そんなの。あるもんでいいよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, who cares? Whatever we've got is fine.”

lines.japanese: こんな優しい目をしたお兄さんなのに、不思議でならない。
lines.english: Strange, when I was such a kind-eyed big brother.

lines.japanese: 「すいませんすいません、しなぞろえ悪くてすいません」
lines.english: “I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I'm sorry the selection is so poor.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、いいっつってんだろテメ。んな細けえこと気にしてんじゃねえよ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “I said it's fine, damn it. Quit sweating every little thing or I'll fucking kill you.”

lines.japanese: こんな優しい言葉もかけちゃうフェミニストなのにな。およそビビられる要素がねえよ。
lines.english: Such a gentleman, always ready with a kind word. Not a scary thing about me.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は逃げるように台所へ戻った。
lines.english: Kobato fled back into the kitchen.

lines.japanese: 俺は首をひねりながらテレビのリモコンを操作する。なんか小鳩の好きそうな芸能人でも出てねえかな。
lines.english: Puzzled, I picked up the remote and started flipping channels. Wasn't there some celebrity on that Kobato liked?

lines.japanese: いや、この際誰でもいい、兄妹の団欒に協力しろ。ああくそ、オモれえのやってねえな……。
lines.english: Hell, at this point, anybody would do. Help a brother and sister enjoy some quality time. Goddamn, there was nothing good on...

lines.japanese: 「ったく……んーだよコレ、朝からしょっぱい電波ばっか流しやがって、この糞テレビ局どもが。ふざけんじゃねえ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “The hell is this...? Nothing but miserable crap on the air first thing in the morning. Fucking TV stations. Don’t screw with me. I’ll fucking kill you.”

lines.japanese: 「ひいいい！　ごごごごめんなさい、よく言っておきます！」
lines.english: “Eeeeeek! I-I'm sorry! I'll give them a stern talking-to!”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: なんか台所で悲鳴のような声が聞こえた。なんだ、ゴキブリでも出たのか。
lines.english: I heard something like a scream from the kitchen. What, was there a cockroach in there?

lines.japanese: よし、そういうときこそ頼れる兄貴の出番だな。俺はキッチンめがけ、少年漫画のヒーローのように颯爽と飛びだした。
lines.english: Perfect. This was where her dependable big brother came in. I dashed for the kitchen like the hero of a boys' manga.

lines.japanese: 「許さねえ！　跡形もなくブッ潰してやる！」
lines.english: “I won't let you get away with this! I'll smash you until there's nothing left!”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃああああ世界が平和でありますようにっ！」
lines.english: “Aaaaaah! May peace prevail on Earth!”
